batch_strategy: Select 32 experiments with no pending rows. Freeze the selected IDs and their supplied premeasurement predictions. Prioritize unresolved solvent-response curves, transfer of recent endpoint-specific failures, and a small number of controlled loading diagnostics. Use CW distance as secondary evidence of coverage gaps; do not interpret single-predictor quantile widths as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: Measure m75 at 20/1 and 150 ul. At 50 ul, measured retention falls between 20/1 (3726956d81fe3954e5b7) and 50/1 (28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e). Together with the selected 150-ul 50/1 row, this tests whether that decrease transfers across loading.

Complete the m75 fixed-150-ul pair at 50/1. Its 50-ul measurement, 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e, was much more compact than its acquisition prediction. Repeating the response contrast at another loading can distinguish a reproducible curve from an influential isolated label.

Measure m25 at 20/1 and 150 ul, below the recently measured 50/1 response of 33.94/89.38 mL (74701496b6fc5465eea7). This intermediate anchor locates finish expansion after the large historical underprediction without assuming the current prediction is still erroneous.

Measure m164 at 20/1 and 100 ul. Its fixed-loading anchors rise from 6.00/14.38 mL at 5/1 (9f450a70d44f4384353f) to 28.20/68.68 mL at 50/1 (c9bef93a79964dc6ede1). This resolves curvature in a conjugated ketone region recently underpredicted.

Measure m203 at 20/1 and 50 ul. The 150-ul measurement was 31.00/34.93 mL (66747ae127e03516ffda), a compact elution interval despite a much later acquisition prediction. The model transfers similar endpoints to 50 ul; this tests whether that compact finish persists.

Measure m51 at 10/1 and 50 ul, paired with the selected 5/1 condition. Recent 5/1 at 100 ul was 15.32/29.42 mL (3e78a776ac9b885d378a). The fixed-50-ul pair tests continued tertiary-alcohol retention growth while separating it from loading transfer.

Measure unsaturated aliphatic aldehyde m53 at 20/1 and 100 ul, paired with 50/1. Its measured 2/1 reference is compact (59bbda2fab97a5d45827). Very high CW distance and sparse weak-eluent anchors make this useful for testing transfer beyond aryl carbonyl chemistry.

Measure m53 at 50/1 and 100 ul, completing the selected response pair. The predicted finish grows from about 33 to 49 mL between 20/1 and 50/1. Labels can establish whether this unanchored aldehyde curve grows, plateaus, or decreases rather than borrowing an aryl-carbonyl response.

Measure naphthyl fluorinated diketone m166 at 20/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 10/1 anchor is 4.93/24.15 mL (fc672dc6f3ecc1d0492c). Together with selected 50/1, this tests the predicted onset transition and finish growth at fixed loading.

Measure m166 at 50/1 and 100 ul. The phenyl fluorinated diketone m167 remains compact at 50/1 (f4c58d48258027bb5485), while m166 is predicted near 24/52 mL with high CW distance. This tests whether the larger aromatic environment changes weak-eluent sensitivity.

Measure benzoylacetone m26 at 50/1 and 100 ul. Measured 10/1 at this loading is 7.40/19.89 mL (ba0d2f91eb0b005857f8), and 20/1 at 150 ul remains moderate (c692f211a6366b2f15c2). This extends a high-CW-distance diketone curve alongside m166.

Measure methyl acetoacetate m95 at 50/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 10/1 anchor is 13.90/32.26 mL (45e24a16b44a89653e4b). This weak-eluent endpoint tests finish growth after the recent compact 5/1 result and the steep tert-butyl analogue result.

Measure cyclopropyl beta-ketoester m94 at 10/1 and 150 ul. At 100 ul, measured finish increases from 26.02 mL at 5/1 (a1809a6c4c3ada20bcb0) to 79.67 mL at 20/1 (e3a799d0fa90b649a157). This tests transfer of that steep response to another loading.

Measure para-fluoroacetophenone m34 at 50/1 and 50 ul. The recent matched-loading 20/1 measurement was 16.75/31.88 mL (6ac700cf79bf6e05982e), above its acquisition prediction. This establishes the weak-eluent continuation in a common aryl-ketone family.

Measure meta-methylacetophenone m41 at 50/1 and 50 ul, extending measured 20/1 at 10.32/20.73 mL (b4d9d000145f0dfcee50). This high-CW-distance endpoint constrains positional-substitution transfer among acetophenones while retaining their recorded loading-solvent differences.

Measure para-methylacetophenone m32 at 50/1 and 50 ul. Its 20/1 finishes differ across loading, including 13.48 mL at 100 ul (ee5c9d29ed57c3312389) and 20.35 mL at 150 ul (8dce8486dfe67a190d0d). This anchors weak-eluent behavior without inferring it from one loading.

Measure seven-membered cyclic ketone m179 at 50/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 20/1 response is 6.13/23.54 mL (8b8becd233748ccae9e3), while the smaller-ring m180 reaches 22.75/48.88 mL at 50/1 (52348febee6695107c49). This tests ring-environment transfer.

Measure bromonaphthaldehyde m196 at 50/1 and 100 ul, beyond measured 20/1 at 6.13/24.44 mL (ffa53b3aa054bc392704). The model predicts relatively little onset growth. This tests whether bromine placement and its carbonyl environment support that response.

Measure para-tert-butyl methyl benzoate m100 at 50/1 and 50 ul. Its measured 5/1 high-loading condition is compact (f8001b01afa2fc47bc39), but the weak-eluent prediction has substantial finish expansion and high CW distance. This extends coverage of remote-substituted aromatic esters.

Measure long-chain acrylate m18 at 50/1 and 150 ul, matched in loading to compact measured 5/1 (89a9ddf69304993652d5). Its high CW distance supports testing whether the ester retains a modest response in weak eluent despite its large lipophilic substituent.

Measure ether-containing acrylate m20 at 5/1 and 50 ul. The same-loading 10/1 reference is 23.78/34.90 mL (5695d3c04943153386bb). This high-CW-distance intermediate tests whether adding an accessible ether changes the acrylate response compared with compact lipophilic esters.

Measure para-aminobenzoate m86 at 2/1 and 100 ul, below measured 5/1 at 28.73/57.53 mL (3ccd6444c8a55917fbf8). This locates the onset of its steep response and complements the meta-amino selection, without treating their different loading-plug volumes as controlled.

Measure meta-aminobenzoate m88 at 2/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 1/1 finish is about 17 mL and 5/1 finish about 62 mL (f863? no measured citation used here; d2921349ba8d9cef15a4 supplies the 5/1 anchor). This fills a high-CW-distance transition in amino-ester chemistry.

Measure phenol-ether m209 at 10/1 and 50 ul, between measured 5/1 at 9.58/16.44 mL (534afc6bd39a8f7923d8) and 20/1 at 26.92/53.89 mL (1b4be0410f927930d56e). This tests the predicted delayed onset transition in a distinct hydroxyl environment.

Acquire an independent catalog row for m81 at the same recorded 10/1, 150-ul conditions as 7d402b3fad455f06fe68. Its short measured finish contrasts with the model's nearly loading-invariant predictions. Replication tests whether the loading association recurs despite conflicting 20/1 labels.

Acquire an independent m92 EA-loaded 1/1, 50-ul row matching 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b. The PE-loaded counterpart e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2 finished 8.56 mL later. Replication is needed before interpreting that single-pair difference as a reproducible solvent association.

Measure m92 at 1/1 and 150 ul with the same EA loading solvent and 200-ul plug as the selected 50-ul replicate. This tests loading transfer within EA conditions, helping distinguish a solvent-associated difference from endpoint-specific loading variation.

Measure m51 at 5/1 and 50 ul, establishing the fixed-loading reference for selected 10/1. Comparison with the measured 100-ul result (3e78a776ac9b885d378a) also tests whether the recent onset overprediction was a loading-transfer problem or an overly steep solvent-response estimate.

Measure side-chain ether-aldehyde m59 at 20/1 and 100 ul. Measured same-loading anchors are 12.70/20.71 mL at 10/1 (fde9781e6b15ffbe093f) and 39.98/64.50 mL at 50/1 (85591a54c419ed02c5f5). This resolves a high-CW-distance response transition.

Measure alpha-hydroxyester m99 at 5/1 and 150 ul, below measured 10/1 at 34.78/57.44 mL (7bbdec21c428010dd67b). This tests the response onset in a hydrogen-bonding ester environment after a large historical underprediction at the higher ratio.

Measure m117 at 10/1 and 150 ul. The recent 50-ul result is ordinary (09c2a4beb05ca5c84aab), whereas 100 ul has a late, slightly reversed-endpoint label (a7bc3fb68bdecbbe086f). This limited diagnostic tests how far that unusual onset should transfer across loading.

Measure ortho-fluorobenzonitrile m163 at 20/1 and 100 ul. Recent 50/1 at 50 ul reached 24.86/44.05 mL (fe212637596386c24049), while 5/1 at 100 ul remains moderate. This high-CW-distance intermediate locates growth and tests transfer from the brominated nitrile.

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent sensitivity depends strongly on structural environment. Recent m25 and m164 measurements show substantial retention growth, whereas m68 and m91 remain much more compact. Acceptor counts, carbonyl counts, or lipophilicity alone do not justify a shared retention correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate anchors and contrasting weak-eluent endpoints can teach graph-condition interactions and prevent corrections learned from strongly retained scaffolds from spreading to compact compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which remaining diketone, beta-ketoester, aldehyde, nitrile, and ester curves grow steeply, and where do their onset and finish transitions occur?

hypotheses.content: Measured retention decreases from 20/1 to 50/1 for m75 at 50 ul and for m127 at both 50 and 150 ul. For m127, finish decreases similarly across those loadings while onset changes strongly with loading. Reproducibility of the m75 decrease across loading remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A second loading contrast can distinguish reproducible nonmonotonic recorded responses from isolated variation. This matters because imposing universal monotonic retention growth could worsen predictions for these rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m75 also decrease between 20/1 and 50/1 at 150 ul, and do onset and finish preserve the same relationship?

hypotheses.content: Loading associations are endpoint- and scaffold-dependent. The m13 intermediate-loading onset was well predicted while finish stayed nearly unchanged. For m81, short high-loading finishes recur at 2/1, 5/1, and 10/1, but conflicting identical-input 20/1 labels limit a deterministic explanation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A targeted independent row can test an association the nearly loading-invariant predictions may miss, while constraining how much unexplained variation should influence learned loading relationships. Sample volume and density-times-volume amount remain coupled.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does another m81 10/1, 150-ul row reproduce the short finish or move toward the longer lower-loading results?

hypotheses.content: The recorded m92 1/1 loading-solvent pair associates PE loading with later onset and finish than EA loading, but one pair does not establish a reproducible solvent effect. Other identical-input m92 records show endpoint variation, making replication and loading-response measurements valuable.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model underestimated the measured solvent-pair difference. Testing its reproducibility can improve use of the recorded loading-solvent feature without fitting a broad rule to a single contrast.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does an independent EA-loaded 50-ul row remain near the earlier result, and how does the EA response change at 150 ul?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl-containing scaffolds require separate calibration of onset and finish. The hindered tertiary alcohol m203 has a much more compact finish response than predicted, whereas other alcohol environments show substantial growth. A common alcohol-based shift is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Contrasting tertiary alcohol, phenol-ether, and hydroxyester responses can teach when onset growth accompanies finish growth and when the elution interval instead contracts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m203 retain its compact 20/1 interval at 50 ul, and do fixed-loading m51 measurements support continued growth between 5/1 and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Late or narrow recorded regimes do not transfer uniformly across loading or adjacent solvent ratios. The m117 10/1 onset spike did not recur at 50 ul, the m133 2/1 late regime did not recur at 100 ul, and m73 returned to ordinary retention at 2/1 and 50 ul. Their causes remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Limited diagnostics can prevent unusual labels from generating broad, inaccurate loading or solvent-response relationships. Missing metadata or measurement variation remain possibilities rather than established explanations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m117 10/1 and 150 ul, is onset closer to the ordinary 50-ul result or the late 100-ul result?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest outcomes strengthen scaffold-specific calibration and weaken broad weak-eluent corrections. m25 and m164 finished substantially later than their acquisition predictions, whereas m68 and m203 were much more compact. The compact m91 weak-eluent result was approximately predicted. These contrasts motivate intermediate anchors for growing curves and measurements in structurally related but unresolved environments.

The m127 150-ul pair reproduced the 20/1-to-50/1 finish decrease previously seen at 50 ul, while onset shifted much earlier at higher loading. The new m75 pair also decreased between 20/1 and 50/1, but currently only at one loading. I therefore allocate a matched second-loading pair to m75. Conversely, m110 at 5/1 finished earlier than its measured 10/1 condition, rejecting the proposed finish dip inferred from predictions; its broader curve now needs less immediate attention.

Loading feedback is more selective. The m13 intermediate-loading measurement closely matched its acquisition prediction, reducing urgency for further nearby interpolation. The m81 2/1 high-loading finish supports the previously observed short finishes at 5/1 and 10/1, but conflicting identical-input 20/1 labels still require caution. The m92 solvent pair produced a larger finish difference than predicted, so I seek an independent EA row before treating the contrast as reproducible.

The m117 and m133 unusual onset regimes failed to recur at the newly measured loading levels, and m73 at 2/1 was ordinary. I reduce emphasis on these anomalies to one discriminating m117 measurement. All cited prediction errors are historical acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch combines response-curve repair with exploration of uncovered structure-condition relationships. Fixed-loading pairs for m75, m51, m53, and m166 distinguish competing response shapes. Intermediate m25, m164, m59, and m163 measurements connect measured anchors across large retention changes. Weak-eluent measurements extend dense catalog families of aromatic ketones and esters while also testing aliphatic aldehyde, long-chain acrylate, cyclic ketone, and amino-ester environments.

Endpoint-specific learning is central: m203 tests whether a compact finish transfers across loading, and m81 receives an independent catalog row to assess its recurring high-loading finish reduction. The two m92 selections test reproducibility and loading transfer after the observed solvent-pair difference. These loading contrasts cannot separate sample-volume effects from density-times-volume amount, and comparisons across molecules retain their recorded solvent and plug-volume differences.

Only one slot follows a localized onset anomaly because unexplained variation may limit its transferable information. High CW distance supports several otherwise scientifically motivated selections; it is not treated as proof of error. Frequent zero lower V2 quantiles and quantile crossing further discourage interpreting the supplied spreads as calibrated uncertainty. The expected benefit is better graph-condition interactions, more accurate onset and finish calibration, and less inappropriate transfer of large corrections across the Row-distribution.
